create.name: Jeffrey S. Reid
create.bio:
Jeffrey S. Reid, whose Daoist name is Li Mao Zihe, is a sixteenth-generation disciple in the Wudang Sanfeng lineage of Daoism. He grew up in Rhode Island, found the Zhuangzi as a teenager and began Chinese martial arts in Providence. At 23 he left for the Wudang Mountains in China, where Master Yuan Xiugang accepted him as a disciple. He stayed for about seven years, training in kung fu, taiji and inner alchemy alongside chanting, scripture study and Mandarin, and from 2009 he captained the mountain's international traditional class.

After coming down from Wudang in 2014 he spent several years as a travelling teacher in different countries, then settled in Santa Cruz, California, in 2018 and opened Wudang Santa Cruz. The school holds weekly classes in Northern Longfist kung fu, taiji, qigong and the internal arts of baguazhang and xingyiquan, for adults and children, and he leads weapons workshops there and teaches abroad. He pairs discipline with humour and asks students to test the tradition in their own bodies rather than take it on trust. His book Leaving the Mountains (Three Pines Press, 2025) follows his lineage from its medieval roots through the Cultural Revolution to today, part history and part memoir. At Esalen he teaches Daoist sleep practices with the scholar Simon Cox.

courses.title: Sleep Alchemy: Secrets of Daoist Sleep Practices for Inner Peace and Renewal
courses.description: A five-day residential workshop at Esalen in Big Sur, taught with Simon Cox. It treats sleep and dreaming as a practice in the Wudang Daoist tradition, with introductory Wudang methods for settling into rest and some of the lore behind them, taught in a light-hearted way.

courses.title: Wudang Kungfu Classes
courses.description: Weekly adult classes in the Wudang Northern Longfist system at his school on Swift Street in Santa Cruz. Training covers stances, kicks, forms and weapons, building flexibility and coordination within a Daoist frame. The first month comes with a money-back guarantee.

courses.title: Taiji and Qigong Classes
courses.description: Weekly Wudang taiji sessions with a Sunday qigong class included, held at the Santa Cruz school. The slow forms are taught as a way to come back into the body and quieten the mind, drawing on Daoist ideas of yin and yang and the Five Phases.

courses.title: Neijia Classes: Baguazhang and Xingyiquan
courses.description: A weekly internal martial arts class in Santa Cruz, currently focused on Dragon Body baguazhang with mud-stepping and circle walking. Xingyiquan forms the other half of the programme, and both are taught as a meeting point of martial skill and meditation.

His Esalen programme is co-led with Simon Cox, who is already live on Spiritpedia (simon-cox.json, rank 220) and likely lists the same workshop; possible duplicate offering across the two listings.
Social accounts are the school's (Wudang Santa Cruz), counted because the school is his own and the Instagram account is in his name.
Taiji 13 and Taiji 28 are form demonstrations on the school channel (6 to 8 minutes) rather than spoken teaching; a human may prefer to drop them.
Beyond Theory is a podcast from The Meadows, an addiction-treatment centre; the episode itself is about Daoist ancient wisdom, so it was kept.
Second photo (sword form in the Siwa Oasis, Egypt, from his teacher page) matches the Esalen headshot but is an action shot, not a headshot.
Esalen spells his first name both Jeffrey and Jeffery; his own site uses Jeffrey.
